scope: The judge demo hosted on a rented server: public HTTPS, each owner app as its own Linux user, one driver at a time, and the three stage scenarios run from a browser over the internet.

server.provider: Hetzner Cloud CPX32, Nuremberg (rented by the user)
server.zebrad: 7.0.0-rc.0 x86_64 (pinned from the release SHA256SUMS), own service user

setup.command: rsync of commit 0c03308 to /opt/latch, then LATCH_HOST=162-55-186-88.sslip.io bash deploy/setup.sh
setup.first_run: about 2.5 minutes, then stopped: /usr/local/libexec did not exist (fixed in 0c03308)
setup.certificates: Let's Encrypt for all three names

checks: https://HOST/, https://alice.HOST/, https://bob.HOST/ and /stage return 200 with valid certificates and HSTS.
CSP: an owner app may be framed only by https://HOST; the site frames only the two app origins and may not be framed.
Without the driver lease: a stage control is refused ("Take the controls first."), and so is a press in an owner app.
A control from another Origin is refused.
Isolation proven by Unix users at every trade: each owner reads its own identity file; the other owner gets a permission error, and so does the network process.
Processes: zebrad as latch-zebra, the network and Anvil as latch, the apps as latch-alice and latch-bob; per-trade roots under 0700 bases.
After the crash scenario only the restarted Bob app runs as latch-bob (its old app and signer were killed with the user).
Firewall: only 22, 80 and 443 reach the host; every demo service listens on loopback.

results: Swap 1:46, Bob’s app killed and restarted 1:55, both refund 1:59, each from a fresh trade, driven from a browser over HTTPS.
Zcash: swaps put only two shielded transactions on chain; the refund adds A (20,000-zatoshi transparent output) and R (spends it, 15,000-zatoshi change).
defects_found_and_fixed: setup.sh assumed /usr/local/libexec exists; Ubuntu does not create it.
A checkout copied with rsync kept the copier’s numeric owner; setup.sh now resets /opt/latch to root (except the network’s .local).
The Foundry version check expected "-stable" but the Linux build reports "1.3.1-v1.3.1", so re-runs would re-download Foundry.
The Hetzner Cloud Firewall allowed only SSH at first; the user opened 80 and 443.
limits: One operator runs all three roles on one server; not independent administration.
Isolated regtest chain and local Anvil; no real value.
